acceptance: The launcher of the benchbox-comment-policy-* processes is identified
Peak CPU and wall time of one comment-policy run are measured and recorded
Either the cost is reduced, for example by reusing the venv or serializing concurrent runs, or the measurement shows it is not the cause
description: On 2026-10-08 the host load average reached 13 while four `benchbox-comment-policy-*` Python processes, each running from its own freshly created temp venv, held about 80% CPU apiece. A timed benchmark run needs a 1-minute load below 2.0 and no other process above 50% CPU, so these runs repeatedly made the machine non-quiet; load was still 4 to 6 hours later. The processes' launcher was not identified, and the share of load they account for was not measured. Find what starts them (commit hooks, pre-flight, or CI-style wrappers), whether each run must build a venv, and whether concurrent runs can be serialized or the venv reused.
